s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?

s:
Arrange the following Gupta rulers in chronological order:
A. Kumaragupta I
B. Ramagupta
C. Skandagupta
D. Chandragupta II
x: The order is Ramagupta, Chandragupta II, Kumaragupta I and Skandagupta. Ramagupta’s reign was brief, while Chandragupta II preceded Kumaragupta I and Skandagupta.
tq: Place the less firmly dated brief reign first, then use the established succession.

s: Which one of the following statements regarding Chandragupta II’s western conquests is correct?
o: He defeated Bhanugupta and annexed Bengal.
He defeated Bandhuvarman and annexed coastal Andhra.
He defeated Rudrasimha III and annexed western Malwa and Gujarat.
He defeated Hastivarman and annexed Kanchi.
x: Chandragupta II defeated the Saka ruler Rudrasimha III and annexed western Malwa and Gujarat, thereby reaching the western sea.
tq: Use the ruler–opponent–territory combination to avoid swapped military achievements.

imitated the coins of the Vakatakas
replaced all Gupta gold coins with silver coins
introduced a new currency for the conquered western region
x: After acquiring the western region, Chandragupta II issued silver coins on the Saka model for the new territory.

s:
Consider the following statements about Chandragupta II:
1. He married the Naga princess Kuberanaga.
2. His daughter Prabhavati Gupta married Vakataka Rudrasena II.
3. The marriage alliance helped extend Gupta influence into the Deccan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. Chandragupta II married Kuberanaga, while Prabhavati Gupta married Rudrasena II of the Vakatakas, providing indirect Gupta control in the Deccan.
tq: Treat marriage alliances as political relationships and verify all linked statements.

s: Which one of the following is the correct inscription–information combination?
o:
Allahabad Pillar — Samudragupta’s conquests
Bhitari — repulse of the Hunas

Mehrauli Iron Pillar — Mandsaur silk-weavers’ guild
Mandsaur — Chandragupta II’s Saka coins

Udayagiri — Bhanugupta’s earliest evidence of sati
Eran — Virasena’s record of conquests

Allahabad Pillar — Skandagupta’s Huna victory
